answer: An EigenTrust-style network discounts each peer’s earned reputation exponentially, with a fixed half-life, so influence persists only when honest service is sustained over time. Newly spawned identities—even those labeled sonnet, juniper, or ivory—begin with negligible incoming trust; reciprocity-weighted transitivity cannot manufacture meaningful eigenvector centrality without trusted peers’ endorsements. Their aggregate score therefore stays below the consensus threshold, limiting Sybil capture.
